University final project · May–December 2025

VietJusticIA.

Building a Vietnamese legal-assistance platform.

I built a mobile app for people asking legal questions and a web portal for the lawyers answering consultation requests. My computing project focused on getting the interfaces, document retrieval and live conversations working together.

Platform
React Native mobile app and React web portal
My work
Application development with substantial AI-assisted code generation
Mobile appAnswer flowLawyer portalDevelopment

Mobile app

Finding the source behind an answer.

A reader can ask a question in Vietnamese or search the legal library by title. The library also supports filters such as document type, issuing body and status.

Source entries with a document ID open the same reader from chat. The reader shows the full text, metadata such as the document number and status, and links to related documents when available.

Legal answer pipeline

From a question to its sources.

FastAPI saves each question and its reply in MongoDB, along with the source references. Each retrieval run uses the latest message. The saved history lets readers revisit earlier answers and reopen their sources.

  1. Ask

    Vietnamese question

    The mobile app sends a question to the authenticated chat endpoint.

  2. Find

    Keyword and vector search

    The backend segments the Vietnamese text and combines results from BM25 and Qdrant.

  3. Expand

    Parent passages

    The service uses each match’s parent ID, when present, to fetch a longer passage for context.

  4. Answer

    Gemini and sources

    Gemini drafts a reply from the passages. The backend matches the model’s source titles to document records.

If the backend can’t match any source titles from the model, it lists the retrieved passages as references instead.

How the search index is built

The backend splits legal text from MongoDB into larger passages for context and smaller excerpts for BM25 search. Each excerpt records the ID of its parent passage.

A separate script embeds excerpts with a multilingual sentence model and writes them to Qdrant. It uses its own text splitter and omits the parent IDs. A vector result from that script can’t supply a parent passage on its own.

Lawyer portal

Taking a request into a conversation.

A person selects an available lawyer in the mobile app and sends a request from their profile. The lawyer reviews it in the portal. Once accepted, both participants can read the conversation history and reply.

Administrators have a separate workspace to manage users and legal documents. Keeping those tasks in the web portal leaves the mobile experience focused on the person asking for help.

  1. Request

    Choose a lawyer

    The app sends the request to the selected lawyer. It appears as pending in their portal.

  2. Accept

    Open the conversation

    Accepting the request automatically creates a conversation linked to it.

  3. Talk

    Stay in sync

    The backend saves messages in MongoDB and uses WebSockets for new messages, typing indicators and read receipts.

Development

Connecting the pieces.

I used FastAPI for the backend, Qdrant for document retrieval and WebSockets for chat. The repository includes the mobile app, the React and TypeScript portal, and Playwright tests covering login, administration and lawyer conversations.
